title: Per-vector slot + hybrid batch discount experiment and QSA readiness playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: run a 6-week experiment to validate a hybrid pricing model for embeddings and reranking that combines a per-vector 'slot' unit with volume/batch discounts applicable to high-throughput customers. Deliverables: (1) experiment spec and pricing bands, (2) QSA-ready packet for sales/contract teams, (3) telemetry dashboard to measure unit economics and migration risk, (4) billing prototype and contract language templates.
background: Current asks from enterprise prospects: predictable per-vector economics for rerank-heavy workloads and clearer bulk discount mechanics for ingestion/batch embedding jobs. Existing catalog entries and previous pilots use per-vector and per-request billing variations that make forecasting hard for large customers. This experiment aims to reconcile meterability with simplicity and to produce artifacts that accelerate QSA/CS negotiations.
success_metrics: 10% increase in closed-won rate for >$100k ARR embedding deals during trial
<=5% uplift in gross unit cost compared to baseline on high-batch workloads
Clear contract clause and QSA answers drafted for top 10 security questions (time-to-approve <=7 days)
Telemetry shows 90% of customer embedding volume fits within one of the proposed batch bands
acceptance_criteria: Pricing bands defined (slot price, batch-discount thresholds, effective unit price calculations)
Billing prototype implemented in billing sandbox and validated end-to-end for meter acquisition
QSA packet (security & architecture answers, dataflow diagrams, KMS/HSM notes) reviewed by Security
Sales playbook and contract addendum templates approved by Legal
Experiment dashboard (cost, latency, conversion lift) published in Console for stakeholders
tasks: Finalize slot definition and nomenclature with engineering (what constitutes a 'slot' vs a 'vector')
Model unit economics and simulate customer examples (small, mid, mega-batch) - owner: Finance
Prototype billing metric (custom meter that aggregates vectors and batch windows) - owner: Billing Eng
Prepare QSA packet: system diagram, data retention, encryption, SOC/ISO references - owner: Security
Draft contract addendum with Legal and Sales specifying batch bands and guarantees
Instrument telemetry and add dashboard charts for effective unit price, batch size distribution, and rerank hit-rate
decisions: Use a 30-minute aggregation window for batch qualification to balance cost vs attribution (tentative)
Bundle: charge a base per-slot price + stepped discounts once daily vector count crosses thresholds (3 bands)
Offer a one-time migration credit for early adopters to be decided by Sales Ops (up to 10% of first-month spend)
Security will require explicit KMS reference in addendum and a standard answer for encryption-at-rest for the QSA
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoff: longer aggregation windows increase discount eligibility but may complicate chargeback transparency for customers
Risk: billing prototype complexity could delay rollout and produce metering disputes without a canonical audit log
Operational: requiring KMS/HSM references adds friction for some customers in regulated industries but reduces security review time
Behavioral: offering batch discounts may shift workload patterns, increasing peak load unpredictability for Dedicated pools
